(Publisher only) If true, set the ClickHouse `async_insert=1` server setting so inserts are
buffered server-side. Defaults to false.

wait_for_async_insert.description:
(Publisher only) With `async_insert`, wait for the server to flush before acking. Defaults to
true (durable). False = fire-and-forget: faster, but a crash before flush can drop the batch.

lookup_query.description:
(Publisher only) SELECT for `lookup`, answering with the first row. Write `WHERE id IN
(${payload:id})` to answer a whole batch in one query, matching rows by `id`.

cursor_column.description:
(Consumer only) Read an existing table **non-destructively** and resumably, paging by this
monotonic column (`SELECT … WHERE {cursor_column} > {last} ORDER BY {cursor_column} ASC LIMIT n`)
and persisting the last read value under `cursor_id`.

cursor_id.description:
(Consumer only) Cursor id used to key the persisted resume position. Without it, progress is not
persisted and every restart re-copies from the beginning.

checkpoint_store.description:
(Consumer only) Where to persist the resume cursor. Because ClickHouse is unsuited to per-row
cursor upserts, a durable checkpoint requires an **external** store URL:
- `file:///var/lib/mqb/cursors.json` → local JSON file
- `postgres://user@host/db/table` / `mysql://host/db/table` → external SQL table (table optional)
- `mongodb://host/db/collection` → external MongoDB collection (collection optional)
- `s3://bucket/prefix` (also `gs://`, `az://`, `abfs://`) → cloud object store; creds via env

May embed connection credentials, so it is treated as a secret.

select_columns.description: (Consumer only) Columns to select in `cursor_column` mode. Defaults to `*`.

polling_interval_ms.description: (Consumer only) Polling interval in milliseconds when the table is drained. Defaults to 100ms.

max_polling_interval_ms.description:
(Consumer only) If set, the poll interval backs off exponentially from `polling_interval_ms`
up to this value while drained, resetting on new rows. Unset = constant interval.

request_timeout_ms.description:
Request timeout in milliseconds for ClickHouse HTTP calls (inserts, cursor reads, status).
Unset = no timeout (wait indefinitely), which suits very large batch inserts.

connect_timeout_ms.description: Connection (TCP + TLS handshake) timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 10000ms.

compression.description:
HTTP body compression for inserts and cursor reads (`none`, `gzip`, `lz4`, `zstd`). Applied
as `Content-Encoding` on the request body and negotiated on the response via `Accept-Encoding`.
`lz4`/`zstd` are faster than `gzip`; all are understood natively by ClickHouse. Defaults to `gzip`.

HttpBulkConfig.description:
HTTP APIs that take or return many JSON documents in one request, such as search engines.

As an output, a batch of upserts is sent as one NDJSON or JSON-array body and deletes as a
list of ids; `result` describes how the target reports success. As an input, `read` pages
through a JSON listing by a cursor. With `query` it answers a batch of lookups in one
request. The endpoint knows no product by name.

url.description: Base URL of the target, e.g. `http://localhost:7700`.

headers.description: Headers sent with every request, e.g. `Authorization`. Treated as secrets.

auth.description: Credentials that are fetched or computed per request: an OAuth2 token or AWS SigV4.

upsert.description: (Publisher only) The request that writes documents. An output needs it or `query`.

query.description: (Publisher only) The request that answers lookups. Excludes `upsert` and `delete`.

read.description: (Consumer only) The request that reads a page of documents. Required for an input.

delete.description: (Publisher only) The request that removes documents. Without it a delete message fails.

operation.description: (Publisher only) Template for a message's operation, e.g. `${metadata:postgres.operation}`.

delete_values.description: (Publisher only) Operation values that mean delete. Defaults to `delete` and `d`.

max_request_bytes.description: (Publisher only) Largest request body in bytes; a bigger batch is split. Defaults to 10 MiB.

request_timeout_ms.description: Request timeout in milliseconds. Unset = no timeout.

connect_timeout_ms.description: Connection timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 10000ms.

HttpBulkAuth.description: How `http_bulk` requests are authenticated beyond `headers`. Set at most one field.

oauth2.description: OAuth2 client credentials: a bearer token is fetched, cached and refreshed.

aws_sigv4.description: AWS Signature Version 4 on every request. Needs the `aws` feature.

scope.description: Scopes to ask for, separated by spaces.

service.description: Service name to sign for, e.g. `es` or `aoss`.

access_key.description: Access key id. Unset = the default AWS credential chain.

path.description: Path and query appended to `url`, e.g. `/indexes/books/documents`.

action.description: `ndjson` only: a line sent before each document, e.g. `{"index":{"_id":"${payload:id}"}}`.

envelope.description: `json_array` only: the body around the array, e.g. `{"docs": {documents}}`.

document.description: Template around each document, e.g. `{"doc": {document}, "doc_as_upsert": true}`.

result.description: How the target reports the outcome. Unset = the HTTP status alone decides.

HttpBulkFormat.description: Body shape of an `http_bulk` upsert request.

oneOf.description: One JSON document per line.
One JSON array holding every document.

HttpBulkResult.description: How an `http_bulk` target reports what happened to a request. Set at most one field.

lines.description: The response has one JSON line per document.

items.description: The response is one JSON document holding an array with an entry per document.

job.description: The response names a job that finishes later and is polled.

HttpBulkLines.description: A response with one JSON line per document, in request order.

success.description: JSON pointer to the boolean that is true for a written document, e.g. `/success`.

error.description: JSON pointer to the error text of a rejected document, e.g. `/error`.

HttpBulkItems.description: A JSON response holding an array with one entry per document, in request order.

path.description: JSON pointer to the array, e.g. `/items`. Empty = the response itself is the array.

error.description: JSON pointer to an entry's error text, e.g. `/index/error/reason`. An entry that has it failed.

HttpBulkJob.description: A job the target runs after answering, polled until it ends.

id.description: JSON pointer to the job id in the response, e.g. `/taskUid`.

poll.description: Path polled with GET; `{id}` is replaced by the job id, e.g. `/tasks/{id}`.

status.description: JSON pointer to the job state in the poll response, e.g. `/status`.

succeeded.description: States that mean the job succeeded.

failed.description: States that mean the job failed. Any other state is polled again.

error.description: JSON pointer to the error text of a failed job, e.g. `/error/message`.

timeout_ms.description: How long the job may run before its documents fail as retryable.

HttpBulkQuery.description: The `http_bulk` request that answers a batch of lookups, one answer per message in order.

path.description: Path and query appended to `url`, e.g. `/books/_mget`.

request.description: Template of one message's part of the body, e.g. `{"_id": "${payload:id}"}`.

envelope.description: `json_array` only: the body around the array, e.g. `{"docs": {requests}}`.

responses.description: JSON pointer to the array of answers, e.g. `/responses`. Empty = the response is the array.

value.description: JSON pointer in an answer to the value returned, e.g. `/_source`. Unset = the whole answer.

found.description: JSON pointer in an answer to a boolean; `false` or missing means not found.

error.description: JSON pointer in an answer to its error text. An answer that has it fails its message.

HttpBulkRead.description: The `http_bulk` request that reads one page of documents.

path.description: Path and query. `{cursor}` is the read position and `{limit}` the batch size.

method.description: HTTP method. Defaults to `GET`, or `POST` with a `body`.

body.description: JSON request body; `{cursor}` and `{limit}` are replaced by JSON values.

items.description: JSON pointer to the array of documents, e.g. `/results`. Empty = the response is the array.

cursor.description: Where the next read position comes from. Unset = the number of documents read so far.

cursor_id.description: Cursor id that keys the saved read position. Unset: every start reads all.

checkpoint_store.description: Where the read position is saved, e.g. `file:///var/lib/mqb/cursors.json`.

polling_interval_ms.description: Wait in milliseconds after an empty page. Defaults to 1000ms.

max_polling_interval_ms.description: If set, the wait doubles after each empty page up to this value.

stream.description: Read one open response as `sse` events or `ndjson` lines instead of pages.

HttpBulkCursor.description:
Where an `http_bulk` input takes its next read position from. Set at most one of
`response` and `item`; with neither the position is the number of documents read.

response.description: JSON pointer to the next position in the response, e.g. `/last_seq`. `null` ends the read.

item.description: JSON pointer to the position in the last document of a page, e.g. `/id`.

start.description: Position before the first read. Defaults to `0` for a count, otherwise to `null`.

HttpBulkStream.description: How an `http_bulk` input that reads one open response is cut into messages.

oneOf.description: Server-sent events; the event id is the read position.
One JSON document per line.

HttpBulkDelete.description: The `http_bulk` request that removes documents by id.

path.description: Path and query. With `{ids}` the ids go there, comma-separated; otherwise as a JSON array body.

id_field.description: Top-level payload field holding the document id. Defaults to `id`.

max_ids.description: Most ids in one request. Defaults to 1000.

envelope.description: The body around the id array, e.g. `{"points": {ids}}`.

line.description: One body line per id instead of an array, e.g. `{"delete":{"_id":{id}}}`.

result.description: How the target reports the outcome. Unset = the HTTP status alone decides.

publication.description: Publication name (must already exist; defines which tables are captured).

consume.description:
(Consumer only) What to read: `capture_new` (default, changes only), `capture_all`
(backfill the tables first, then changes) or `snapshot` (backfill only).

source_metadata.description: Include authoritative `mqb.src.postgres_*` source positions. Defaults to false.

slot_name.description: Replication slot name; created if missing when `create_slot` is true.

create_slot.description: Create the replication slot if it does not exist.

create_publication.description:
Create the `publication` if missing (default false; leave off if it pre-exists).
Needs table ownership for `publication_tables`, or superuser when none are set (`FOR ALL TABLES`).

publication_tables.description:
Tables to include when managing the publication (`create_publication`); may be `schema.table`.
Missing ones are added to an existing publication (never removed). Empty = `FOR ALL TABLES` (needs superuser).

temporary_slot.description: Ephemeral run: drop the slot when the route stops. Not restart-safe; a hard crash leaks it.

cursor_id.description: Checkpoint key for the confirmed LSN and backfill progress; defaults to `slot_name`.

checkpoint_store.description: Local file (path or `file://`) for resume state; unset, the slot alone tracks the stream.

status_interval_ms.description: Standby-status-update interval in ms; must be shorter than the server's `wal_sender_timeout`.

tls.description: TLS configuration for the replication connection.

id_hash.description: Hash for change `message_id`s: `fnv1a` (default, keeps existing dedup state) or `sha256`.

PostgresConsume.description:
How a `postgres_cdc` endpoint consumes its publication. The intent-named counterpart of
[`MongoConsume`], so the two CDC endpoints read alike.

`consumer` has no Postgres meaning — a replication slot is not a work queue; use a `sqlx`
endpoint for competing consumers.

oneOf.description:
**Stream changes only** — capture what happens from the slot's position onward. Reads
nothing that already exists; never ends on drain. Default, because it is what
`postgres_cdc` has always done.

**Backfill, then stream** — page the publication's tables by primary key first, then
capture changes, with no gap between the two. The slot is created before the backfill
starts, so the server retains WAL throughout. Delivery across the handover is
at-least-once, so the sink must upsert. Each table needs a single-column primary key.

**One-shot backfill** — page the publication's tables by primary key, then end the
route. Non-destructive, creates no slot, and captures no changes.

IdHash.description: Hash that folds a key into a deterministic 128-bit `message_id`.

oneOf.description: FNV-1a, 128-bit. Default: the ids earlier releases produced, so existing dedup state keeps matching.
First 128 bits of SHA-256. Collision-resistant, but every id changes, so dedup state from `fnv1a` no longer matches.

SequenceConfig.description:
Reads several input endpoints one after another: each is drained before the next
begins, and the last one streams until the route stops.

endpoints.description: The inputs to read, in order. At least one is required.

cursor_id.description:
(Optional) Identifies the durable phase marker, so a restart resumes at the phase
it had reached instead of replaying the earlier ones. Needs `checkpoint_store`.

checkpoint_store.description:
(Optional) Where to persist the phase marker. A local path, `file://`, or any URL
the shared checkpoint stores accept. Without it, every restart begins at phase 1.

StreamBufferConfig.description: Configuration for the correlated in-process stream response buffer.

topic.description: Shared buffer topic used by both the publisher and correlated consumers.

correlation_id.description:
Consumer-only correlation id partition to read from.

Leave this unset for the publisher endpoint configured in
`HttpConfig::stream_response_to`. Set it on consumers so a reader only
receives messages belonging to one request or response stream.

capacity.description: Capacity of each correlation partition. Defaults to 100.

idle_ttl_secs.description: Seconds before a partition with no attached consumer is discarded. 0 disables. Defaults to 3600.

metadata_key.description: Value-lookup mode: the metadata key whose value picks the case.

cases.description: Value-lookup mode: a map of metadata values to endpoints.

when.description: Predicate mode: ordered cases, first match wins. Needs the `filter` feature.

default.description: The default endpoint if no case matches.

SwitchCase.description: One predicate case of a `switch` in `when` mode.

if.description: Expression over payload fields and `meta.<key>`, e.g. `amount > 100`.

RequestForwardConfig.description:
Sends each message to a request-capable endpoint and forwards its response elsewhere.

Turns a request/reply exchange (HTTP, or a request_reply NATS/Mongo/Memory endpoint) into
a one-way flow whose response lands on `forward_to` — e.g. IBM MQ → HTTP → IBM MQ. On
request error/timeout the original message is forwarded instead (unchanged). Successful
responses carry the transport-native status (e.g. `http_status_code`), so a `switch` on
`forward_to` can route them by status; a failed request forwards the original message with
no status key, so catch failures on the switch's default branch.

to.description: The request-capable endpoint to send each message to (e.g. an `http` client).

forward_to.description: Where the response (or, on error, the original message) is forwarded.

DeliveryGuarantee.description:
What a route guarantees about its sink effect, as inferred from its configuration.

Ordered weakest to strongest, so a requirement is met by any guarantee `>=` it.

oneOf.description: The source forgets a message once it hands it over; a crash can lose it.
Acked only after the sink accepted it; a crash or retry can repeat the write.
At-least-once delivery absorbed by an idempotent sink write: the effect lands once.
